What it lacks is exactly the two things you named: **hierarchy** (where am I in the tree) and **ownership** (what is doing which part). Here's how the pieces compose. ## Three layers, one hierarchy | Layer | Owns | Today | |---|---|---| | `todos/` files | the durable tree — items and the map (parent) across sessions | items only; no map shape yet | | **pi-omp `todo` widget** | the in-context slice — current map's children as phases, steps as tasks, one `in_progress` = *where you are*, owner = *who's on it* | phases/tasks/one in-progress; no owner, no nesting, no link to `todos/` | | pi-crumbs | provenance — uncommitted file ops = footprint of the side quest you're in | records `file_op`; no notion of fork | | pi-delegate | executes forks at root — scout/worker/reviewer with run ids | works; nothing shows which task a run is serving | ## The changes, smallest first 1. **`owner` and `ref` on a task** (`src/todo.ts` `TodoItem`, `todo` tool params, widget render). `owner` is `me`, a pi-delegate run label, or a Hop Op id; `ref` is the `todos/` id. The widget then answers \"what is doing what\" at a glance, and the existing rule \"todo calls never travel alone\" extends naturally: a `delegate` launch travels with `todo start <task> owner:<run>`. 2. **`fork` / `return` ops** for the stack. `fork <content>` pushes a phase named `↳ <content>` and marks the parent task in-progress with owner `fork`; `return` completes it and auto-promotes back to the parent — the existing promote logic already does the climb. One level of nesting shown in the widget is enough to answer \"where am I\"; deeper than that is the signal to delegate instead of descend. 3. **Point the round-trip at the map, not `TODO.md`.** `todo.file: \"TODO.md\"` writes a root backlog file, which is now a parallel backlog under our own rule.
